types.title: Adam, the first man
types.note: As the one man's disobedience brought condemnation to all, so the one man's obedience brings righteousness and life to all.

types.title: The marriage of Adam and Eve
types.note: As Eve was taken from Adam's side and presented as his bride, so the church is drawn from Christ's wounded side and presented as His bride.
types.src: SermonIndex, Habershon "Study of the Types" ch. 14

types.title: Abel, the righteous murdered brother
types.note: Abel's acceptable sacrifice and innocent blood prefigure Christ, whose own innocent blood speaks forgiveness rather than vengeance.

types.title: Melchizedek, king-priest of Salem
types.note: A priest-king with no recorded genealogy or end of life prefigures Christ's eternal, non-Levitical priesthood.

types.title: Abraham, the father who offered his son
types.note: As Abraham was willing to offer his "only son" on Moriah, so God the Father gave His only Son for the world.

types.title: Isaac, the promised son on the altar
types.note: The beloved promised son, carrying the wood and bound on the altar, then received back alive, prefigures Christ's death and resurrection.

types.title: The ram caught in the thicket
types.note: The substitute ram God provided in Isaac's place anticipates the Lamb God provided in our place.

types.title: The seed/offspring of Abraham
types.note: God's promise that "in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed" narrows to the single offspring, Christ.

types.title: Jacob's ladder at Bethel
types.note: The stairway joining heaven and earth at "the house of God" prefigures Christ Himself as the meeting place of God and man.

types.title: Joseph, rejected then exalted
types.note: The beloved son betrayed for silver, suffering unjustly, then exalted to save his people from death, mirrors Christ's rejection and glorification.

types.title: Moses, deliverer and prophet
types.note: The mediator who delivered Israel from bondage and spoke God's words prefigures the greater Mediator who delivers from sin.

types.title: Aaron, the high priest
types.note: Aaron, consecrated to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, foreshadows Christ, the appointed and sympathetic High Priest.

types.title: Joshua (Yeshua), successor who gives rest
types.note: The leader named "The LORD saves" who brought Israel into the inheritance prefigures Jesus, who brings His people into true rest.

types.title: David, the shepherd-king
types.note: The shepherd boy anointed king, who slew the giant and whose throne was promised forever, prefigures Christ, the Good Shepherd and eternal Son of David.

types.title: David betrayed by a close friend
types.note: David's betrayal by a trusted companion prefigures Christ's betrayal by Judas at the table.

types.title: The righteous sufferer of the Psalms
types.note: David's vivid sufferings — pierced hands and feet, divided garments, gall and vinegar — are taken up in the NT as the script of Christ's passion.

types.title: Solomon, the glorious son of David
types.note: The wise king of peace who built God's house prefigures the greater Son of David, whose wisdom draws the nations and who builds the true temple.

types.title: Elijah, the rejected prophet taken up
types.note: The prophet who called Israel to repentance, was rejected, fed in the wilderness, raised the dead, and was taken to heaven, prefigures Christ's ministry and ascension.

types.title: Elisha, the prophet of double-portion grace
types.note: The miracle-working successor who cleansed a Gentile leper and multiplied bread prefigures Christ's grace extending beyond Israel.

types.title: Jonah, three days in the deep
types.note: The prophet's descent into death's waters and restoration on the third day prefigures Christ's burial and resurrection.

types.title: Jonah's preaching to Gentile Nineveh
types.note: The prophet whose message brought a pagan city to repentance prefigures the greater Prophet whose gospel gathers the nations.

types.title: Israel, God's firstborn son
types.note: The nation called God's "firstborn son," brought out of Egypt, is recapitulated in Jesus, the true Son, brought out of Egypt.

types.title: The Son of Man in glory
types.note: Daniel's heavenly figure receiving everlasting dominion is claimed by Jesus as His own identity and destiny.

types.title: The tabernacle
types.note: God's portable dwelling among Israel prefigures Christ, in whom God dwells among men, and the heavenly sanctuary He entered.

types.title: The temple
types.note: The house where God's glory dwelt prefigures Christ's body, the true meeting place of God and man, raised on the third day.

types.title: The Aaronic/Levitical priesthood
types.note: The hereditary priesthood offering repeated sacrifices for sin prefigures Christ's superior, permanent priesthood and once-for-all offering.

types.title: The sacrifices of the Law
types.note: Every animal sacrifice, showing that guilt deserves death and only blood atones, prefigures the one sacrifice of Christ that truly takes away sin.

types.title: The burnt offering (wholly consumed)
types.note: The offering wholly consumed on the altar, ascending as a pleasing aroma, prefigures Christ's total self-giving to God.

types.title: The sin offering
types.note: The bull or goat slain outside as the bearer of the people's sin prefigures Christ made sin for us.

types.title: The guilt (trespass) offering
types.note: The ram offered to make restitution for specific guilt prefigures Christ, whose soul was made the guilt offering for His people.

types.title: The peace (fellowship) offering
types.note: The shared sacrificial meal celebrating restored fellowship with God prefigures the peace Christ's blood makes between God and man.

types.title: The grain offering
types.note: The crushed fine flour and frankincense offered to God prefigures Christ, the bruised grain whose death bears much fruit.

types.title: The Passover lamb
types.note: The unblemished lamb whose blood on the doorposts turned away God's judgment prefigures Christ, whose blood shields believers from wrath.

types.title: The Feast of Unleavened Bread
types.note: The week of bread without leaven (sin) following Passover prefigures the sinless life of Christ and the believer's call to holiness.

types.title: The Feast of Firstfruits
types.note: The first sheaf of the harvest offered to God prefigures Christ's resurrection as the first of the great harvest of the righteous.

types.title: The Feast of Weeks (Pentecost)
types.note: The harvest feast fifty days after Passover prefigures the Spirit's outpouring and the great harvest of three thousand souls at the church's birth.

types.title: The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur)
types.note: The high priest's yearly entry with blood into the Most Holy Place prefigures Christ's once-for-all entry into heaven with His own blood.

types.title: The Sabbath day
types.note: The weekly rest from labor prefigures the spiritual rest Christ gives through His finished work.

types.title: Circumcision
types.note: The cutting away of flesh marking covenant membership prefigures the spiritual circumcision of the heart accomplished in Christ.

types.title: The (new) covenant sealed with blood
types.note: As Moses sealed the old covenant with sacrificial blood, so Christ's blood seals the promised new covenant of forgiven sins.

types.title: The Law as guardian and shadow
types.note: The whole Mosaic system, guarding and foreshadowing, was designed to lead sinners to Christ, its substance.

types.title: The Davidic covenant and kingship
types.note: The everlasting throne promised to David's seed is fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David who reigns forever.

types.title: The prophetic office ("a prophet like Moses")
types.note: The office of God's spokesman, culminating in the promised Prophet, is fulfilled in Christ, God's final Word.

types.title: The cities of refuge
types.note: The cities where the manslayer fled from the avenger prefigure Christ, the refuge to whom guilty sinners flee for safety.

types.title: The kinsman-redeemer law
types.note: The near kinsman legally qualified to buy back what was lost prefigures Christ, who became our Kinsman to redeem us.

types.title: The anointing (Messiah = "Anointed One")
types.note: Priests and kings consecrated with oil prefigure Jesus, the Anointed One consecrated by the Spirit for His threefold office.

types.title: The continual (daily) burnt offering
types.note: The lamb offered every morning and evening prefigures Christ's single offering, which needs no repetition.

types.title: The bronze serpent on the pole
types.note: Dying Israelites healed by looking at the lifted serpent prefigure sinners saved by looking in faith to the lifted-up Christ.

types.title: Manna, bread from heaven
types.note: The heaven-sent bread that sustained Israel daily prefigures Christ, the true bread from heaven who gives eternal life.

types.title: The smitten rock that gave water
types.note: The rock struck so that water flowed for a thirsty people prefigures Christ, struck in judgment, from whom living water flows.

types.title: Noah's ark
types.note: The one vessel of wood in which all who entered were saved from judgment prefigures Christ, the one refuge from God's wrath.

types.title: The ark of the covenant
types.note: The gold-covered chest bearing God's presence and the tablets of the Law prefigures Christ, in whom God's presence and perfect obedience dwell.

types.title: The mercy seat (atonement cover)
types.note: The golden lid where sacrificial blood was sprinkled before God's glory prefigures Christ, the place where God's justice and mercy meet.

types.title: The veil of the tabernacle/temple
types.note: The curtain barring access to God's presence prefigures Christ's flesh, torn in death to open the way into the Holy of Holies.

types.title: The altar of burnt offering
types.note: The bronze altar where substitutionary sacrifices burned prefigures the cross, the altar of Christ's once-for-all sacrifice.

types.title: The pillar of cloud and fire
types.note: God's guiding, sheltering presence leading Israel through the wilderness prefigures Christ's presence guiding His people.

types.title: The red heifer's ashes
types.note: The unblemished red heifer burned outside the camp, whose ashes cleansed from death's defilement, prefigures Christ sacrificed outside the gate to cleanse the conscience.

types.title: The scapegoat (for Azazel)
types.note: The live goat bearing the people's sins into the wilderness prefigures Christ carrying our sins away, "as far as the east is from the west."

types.title: The tree of life
types.note: The life-giving tree barred after the fall is restored in Christ, through whom access to eternal life is reopened.

types.title: The table of showbread (bread of the Presence)
types.note: The twelve loaves continually before God's face prefigure Christ, the Bread of God's presence sustaining His people.

types.title: The golden lampstand
types.note: The seven-branched lamp giving light in the Holy Place prefigures Christ, the true Light shining in God's house.

types.title: The altar of incense
types.note: The perpetual incense ascending before God's throne prefigures Christ's unceasing intercession for His people.

types.title: The door of the tabernacle
types.note: The single curtained entrance into God's dwelling prefigures Christ as the only way into God's presence.

types.title: The cornerstone
types.note: The rejected stone made the chief foundation stone prefigures Christ, rejected by men but made the foundation of God's building.

types.title: The foundation stone
types.note: God's promised sure foundation in Zion prefigures Christ, the tested stone on which faith rests securely.

types.title: The key of David
types.note: The steward's key of supreme household authority prefigures Christ's absolute authority over God's house and the kingdom.
types.src: NT's own explicit citation. Note: prophecy applied rather than type proper

types.title: The Flood
types.note: The waters that judged the world while lifting the ark prefigure baptism, in which believers pass through judgment into new life.

types.title: The Exodus from Egypt
types.note: God's redemption of Israel from slavery through blood and water prefigures Christ's greater redemption of His people from sin and death.

types.title: The Red Sea crossing
types.note: Israel's passage through the waters, buried to Egypt and raised to freedom, prefigures Christian baptism into Christ.

types.title: The wilderness wanderings and testings
types.note: Israel's forty years of testing, which they failed, are recapitulated in Christ's forty days of testing, which He passed as the faithful Son.

types.title: The conquest of Canaan
types.note: Under Joshua, Israel's victories over its enemies and entry into the inheritance prefigure Christ's victory over spiritual enemies, leading His people into the heavenly inheritance.

types.title: Sinai and the giving of the Law
types.note: The terrifying mountain of law and its mediator Moses prefigure, by contrast, the greater mountain of grace and its Mediator, Christ.

types.title: Bethlehem
types.note: The little town of David's birth becomes the birthplace of David's greater Son, the promised Ruler.
types.src: NT's own explicit citation. Note: direct prophecy-fulfillment

types.title: Egypt (the sojourn and return)
types.note: As Israel, God's son, was called out of Egypt, so Jesus, the true Son, recapitulates the exodus in His own infancy.

types.title: Jerusalem / Mount Zion
types.note: The earthly city where God put His name prefigures the heavenly Jerusalem, the eternal dwelling of God with His redeemed people in Christ.

types.title: Canaan, the promised land
types.note: The earthly inheritance flowing with milk and honey prefigures the heavenly country and the Sabbath rest Christ secures.

types.title: Thirty pieces of silver
types.note: The price paid to betray Jesus — thirty pieces of silver thrown into the temple — fulfills Zechariah's wages, cast to the potter in the house of the LORD.

types.title: Pierced for our transgressions
types.note: The soldier's spear in Jesus' side fulfills Zechariah: 'they shall look on me whom they have pierced.'

types.title: David's Lord at God's right hand
types.note: Jesus turns David's own psalm — 'The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand' — into proof that the Christ is more than David's son.
